why_now: Over the last two quarters the company stepped up its 2026 optical data-centre outlook three times (Keystone USD 100-130 million in Jan, optical USD 150-170 million in Apr, USD 210-230 million in Jul), Q2 revenue was USD 168.8 million (+55% y/y) with infrastructure +145%, Q3 is guided to USD 210-220 million (about +27% q/q at the midpoint), GAAP profit returned in Q2 and gross margin guidance reached about 60% non-GAAP. The revolver was extended to 2028. The stock moved from about USD 17 in April to USD 106, so the question now is how much of a multi-year optical ramp is already in the price.
thesis: MaxLinear is a fabless mixed-signal company that, per its filings, has pivoted from cable broadband toward AI data-centre optical interconnect (Keystone 5 nm PAM4 DSP at 800G, next Rushmore at 1.6T). Q2 2026 filings are consistent with a real inflection: infrastructure revenue up 145% y/y, a guided Q3 step to USD 210-220 million, and non-GAAP operating margin of 22% rising toward about 28% on guidance arithmetic. The asymmetric-opportunity test is price and durability: about USD 10.5 billion of equity value, about 12x annualised Q3 sales, with the optical growth concentrated in a handful of customers, a 2023-24 history of a 48% revenue fall, and Rushmore timing that has moved out by 2-3 quarters. The evidence suggests it is a high-quality-looking AI-supply-chain second-order beneficiary whose upside is real but already partly priced; interesting for monitoring, not yet an asymmetric entry candidate.
multibagger_mechanism: A plausible path to a further 2-3x in 24 months is: (1) Keystone 800G keeps taking share at module makers serving US and Asian hyperscalers, lifting optical to well above the USD 210-230 million 2026 outlook (e10, e11), (2) Rushmore 1.6T plus Washington and Annapurna add revenue from H2 2027 with higher ASPs (e10), (3) gross margin moves from about 60% to the 65% goal (e10), and (4) operating leverage on opex of about USD 70 million a quarter lifts non-GAAP EPS toward USD 4-5, with the market still paying 45-60x. Reverse arithmetic says 3x needs about USD 3.4 billion of revenue at a constant multiple (e31), so a plausible chain reaches 2-3x only if revenue approaches roughly USD 1.4-1.5 billion at about 62% gross margin and the multiple holds, which depends on links management has not committed to dates (Rushmore revenue 2027 H2, e34).
expectations_gap: At USD 105.93 the market cap is about USD 10.5 billion (e30). At a 35x non-GAAP multiple and a 26% net margin that is consistent with roughly USD 1.15 billion of revenue, about 1.35x the Q3-guided run-rate (e31): the price seems to assume the optical ramp continues into 2027 and the 2027 Rushmore ramp starts on schedule, but not yet a multi-billion-dollar business. On GAAP the multiple is about 136x annualised, and non-GAAP excludes stock compensation of about 17% of revenue. Evidence suggests the gap to a 3x outcome is large; the evidence is more consistent with a 1-2x range if the ramp executes, and a deep drawdown if hyperscaler orders pause.

bull_case.name: bull
bull_case.description: Model estimate: Keystone share gains continue, Rushmore ramps from H2 2027 and Washington/Annapurna add content, revenue run-rate near USD 1.4-1.5 billion by 2027 exit at about 62% gross margin and about 38% non-GAAP operating margin, EPS about USD 4.5-5, with a 45-60x multiple retained. Probability is modest because both earnings and multiple have to stay elevated.

base_case.name: base
base_case.description: Model estimate: guided Q3 is met, 2027 revenue about USD 1.0-1.1 billion with gross margin about 60-61%, non-GAAP EPS about USD 3, Rushmore starts H2 2027, and a 30-40x multiple gives roughly 0.8-1.5x of today's price. Highest probability because filings and guidance point to growth that the price already largely discounts.

bear_case.name: bear
bear_case.description: Model estimate: an AI optical digestion, a customer concentration shock or a Rushmore delay pushes revenue back toward USD 600-650 million, gross margin to about 57%, non-GAAP EPS under USD 1.2 and the multiple to 25-35x; inventory and purchase obligations then pressure cash. The stock has already fallen about 48% in four weeks (July 2026) and was USD 17 in April.

risks: Valuation: about 12x EV/annualised Q3 guided sales and about 47x annualised non-GAAP EPS (136x on GAAP) at USD 105.93 after a 6.4x rise in twelve months and 8.3x from the 52-week low (e16, e30); a 3x from here needs about USD 3.4 billion of revenue at a constant 35x non-GAAP multiple (e31).

Cyclicality: revenue fell from USD 693 million in FY2023 to USD 361 million in FY2024 (about -48%) in the last downturn; the company itself says revenue will fluctuate 'consistent with the cyclical nature of our industry' (e3, 10-Q) and customers buy on purchase orders (e6).

AI/optical concentration: the 2026 optical outlook of USD 210-230 million is roughly 29% of my approximate 2026 revenue and nearly all of infrastructure's growth; ramps depend on a handful of module makers and hyperscalers whom management declines to name (e10, e32).

Competition in PAM4 DSP: Broadcom, Marvell, Credo, MACOM, Semtech and vertically integrated module makers are named competitors and are larger or better resourced; the optical share is not disclosed so the 'share gain' claim cannot be checked against filings (e4, e10).

Working capital and supply: inventory USD 105.5 million, 123 days, purchase obligations USD 221 million (USD 165 million due H2 2026) and rising wafer prepayments; operating cash flow was negative in H1 2026 (USD -4.1 million) despite rising profit, and foundry/OSAT costs are rising (e7, e10).

Legal overhang: Silicon Motion SIAC arbitration (damages claimed not disclosed), new California fraud complaint filed 14 May 2026, Ninth Circuit appeal; an adverse result could strain liquidity against an USD 80 million minimum-liquidity covenant (e8, e13).

Quality of earnings: GAAP operating margin was still negative in Q2 (-2.5%) because stock-based compensation (USD 27.5 million) and performance equity (USD 9.2 million) are excluded from non-GAAP; stock-based pay rose sharply with the share price, so dilution is a real cost (diluted count 97.3 million in Q2, 99 million guided) (e9).

Governance signals: auditor dismissed in May 2026 (no disagreements reported, e14); the CEO is also Chairman; insider sales (Form 4/144 filings in Aug 2026 exist) were not analysed. Not verified: proxy statement, replacement auditor, executive ownership.

Not verified: no sell-side consensus read (expectations gap relies on reverse arithmetic only); competitor financials (Marvell, Broadcom, Credo) not read; MaxLinear IR site and webcast not accessed so transcripts came from a third-party host.

exit_rules.condition: The 2026 optical data-centre revenue outlook is cut below the USD 210 million low end, or Q4 2026 revenue is guided below the Q3 2026 actual, or infrastructure revenue falls sequentially in any quarter from the USD 85.0 million of Q2 2026.
Non-GAAP gross margin below 56% in any quarter (guided 58.5-61.5% for Q3) or non-GAAP operating margin below 15% with revenue above USD 200 million per quarter.
No Rushmore (1.6T) production revenue recognised by the Q4 2027 report (expected about Jan 2028), or a further slip in management's timing statements beyond H2 2027.
Days of inventory above 140 (123 in Q2 2026) together with a sequential revenue decline, or inventory purchase obligations above USD 250 million while revenue guidance is flat or lower.
EV above 20x annualised latest-quarter revenue (about USD 17 billion at USD 215 million a quarter) without an optical outlook raise.
A Silicon Motion arbitration award or accrual that exceeds USD 100 million, or any covenant breach / waiver disclosed (net leverage above 3.5x or liquidity below USD 80 million).
A weekly close below USD 70 (about 34% under the 2026-10-02 price, near the Aug-Sept 2026 sampled range of USD 57-75) triggers an emergency thesis review rather than an automatic exit.

The company has no long-term customer purchase commitments (e6) and its FY2023-FY2024 history shows a roughly 48% revenue drop in a downturn (e3). With 6 months of visibility and an optical hyperscaler base of 'a handful of customers', a pause would show up quickly.
